Cast = Fish Wrangler 3D's own coach voices, made with FW's Steam-trailer recipe: Gemini 2.5 PRO TTS, director notes fenced off from the words, the drawl SPELLED into the text (fer, yer, an'), sped up afterwards. 'Diego' is spelled Dee-AY-go in Earl's lines or his twang says 'Did I go'.

diego.style: Character: a rowdy old Appalachian mountain redneck fishing-boat deckhand. Thick lazy hillbilly drawl, sloppy and slurred, words mashed together, dropped endings, a little hoarse, grinning ear to ear. Fast, loud and excited, never careful or precise. Words in square brackets are delivery cues, not words.

earl.style: Cousin Earl, a heavy-set old Gulf Coast hillbilly mechanic and welder who lives next to a yacht on cinder blocks. He is FUNNY: grumpy, dry, put-upon, every line has comic timing - a beat before the punchline, landing it flat like he does not know it is a joke. ACCENT: a THICK Southern redneck twang - nasal, every vowel stretched and bent, dropped g's, the twang the whole point of the voice. Grumbly, a little gravel. Medium pace, lazy rhythm.

slides: Well howdy, y'all! Deckhand Diego here. Today yer gonna learn ya can build anything. I'm sure of it. Mostly sure.
He ain't been sure o' nothin' since the day he was born.
Engineers break stuff... on purpose! Now that's my kinda job!
Rockets blow up so the next one don't. Same thing happens to my boats.
Three tries! The first one crawled like a turtle. The second one wobbled. The third one... she flies!
Two outta three bein' bad. That's a good Tuesday 'round here.
A.I. read the whole internet, an' now it just guesses the next word. Like guessin' where the catfish are!
An' it's wrong 'bout as often as Dee-AY-go.
Talkin' to A.I. is like tellin' yer fishin' buddy what ya want. What, details, rules... then check his work!
Always check his work. Trust me.
Type it. Print it. Hold it. Kai made this motor holder outta nothin' but words. I use a welder.
The A.I. finds the parts an' drops 'em right in the shoppin' cart!
An' a grown-up still pushes the buy button. That's the important part.
Back in my day, instructions came in a language nobody spoke. Now the robot draws 'em, LEGO style, one step at a time.
Nine volts'd fry that little brain like a hush puppy. Two resistors shrink it down to a tiny sip it can read.
Drivin' the boat is a video game now! Fire the lasers!
Them ain't lasers, Dee-AY-go. Them's blinkin' lights.
Rocket builders, game makers, doctors, architects. Ever' kind of engineer's got a robot buddy now.
Safety first! Never tell an A.I. yer full name, yer school, or where ya live.
An' ask a grown-up 'fore ya plug anything in. Ask me how I know.
Yer turn, y'all! Write yer own A.I. message. What, details, rules... an' check it!
Weirder'n Dee-AY-go, if ya can manage it.
